clue.text: Follow case which involves leading opposition MPs

parts.note: to shadow someone is to follow them closely
a cabinet is a case or cupboard for storing things

explanation.surface: A detective trails a suitcase linked to senior politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shadow Cabinet is the group of senior MPs from the main opposition party in the UK Parliament, each watching a government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the opposition's front bench of spokespeople is formally called by this name.

clue.text: Interactive worker takes on boy

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a son is a boy, someone's male child

explanation.surface: An employee takes on a young lad to help with the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical approach that involves direct participation rather than watching is described with this hyphenated term.

clue.text: Day to get late letters from wimp

parts.note: the letters on a gravestone for someone late, i.e. dead, are those of requiescat in pace

explanation.surface: A day when letters arrive late from a feeble correspondent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead here, and RIP (rest in peace) is the set of letters carved on a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a weak, ineffectual person is called a drip, a synonym for a wimp.

clue.text: The Spanish support wife over right of singer

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' tells us to turn the preceding run of words upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman's bra and her husband are somehow tied up with a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns EL + BRA + W into WARBLE; then R (right) is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbler is a small songbird, so it is a singer of the bird world.

clue.text: Liven up a pal from Ulster?

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster
a mate is a pal or friend

explanation.surface: A question of whether a friend from Northern Ireland might cheer people up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, loosely equated with Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to bring energy or life to something, a synonym of enliven.

clue.text: Move slowly in mountain chain

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the join between them

explanation.surface: Climbers make slow progress across a range of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward a little at a time is to proceed very gradually.

clue.text: English PM adopts man's title

indicators.note: the prime minister's name takes in the other piece, as a parent adopts a child into the family

parts.note: Pitt (either the Elder or the Younger) was a British Prime Minister
he is the pronoun for a man; 'man's' reads as 'man is'

explanation.surface: A British prime minister takes on a man's honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' signals a container: the man goes inside the PM. William Pitt the Elder and the Younger were both British Prime Ministers, a favourite crossword PM.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or byname added to a person's name, a kind of title.

clue.text: Feel for odd one abandoning botany, say, in time of flowering

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of the first two words are put into a strange order
the scientific discipline lets go of a letter, abandoning it

parts.note: botany is an example of a science
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone senses something strange as a single person gives up plant studies during the blooming season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges FEEL FOR into EFFLORE; 'abandoning' takes I from SCIENCE, leaving SCENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany efflorescence is the process or period of blossoming.

clue.text: The car could go over safely here when the sea's not rough?

definitions.text: The car could go over safely here when the sea's not rough?

parts.words: The car could go over safely here when the sea's not rough?
parts.note: read as a calm (level) sea being a safe one to sail across, while really it describes where a road meets a railway

explanation.surface: Advice on when a car ferry can safely make the trip across calm water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ferry crossing on a flat, calm sea; in fact it is the place where a car drives over a railway line at the same level.
explanation.definitionFit: A level crossing is where a road crosses a railway at grade, a spot where cars pass over the track.

clue.text: Banker drops in to see connoisseur

indicators.note: the banking word lets go of the following two letters, dropping them

parts.note: a financier is a banker or money man

explanation.surface: A bank employee pops in to visit an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a classic disguise for a river in crosswords, but here it is a financier who loses IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancier is an enthusiast with expert knowledge, such as a pigeon fancier.

clue.text: way

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held only as 'way' (7): the rest of the clue is missing from the OCR text and no source found gives it.

clue.text: Form loses conservative girl

indicators.note: the school year group loses a letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A school class loses a traditionalist pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a Scots and northern English word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Related group got round Spain without mishap

indicators.note: the family group surrounds the abbreviation, getting round it

parts.note: a clan is a group of related families
E (España) is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A family travelled around Spain and had no accidents.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean getaway or clean finish is one achieved without error or trouble.

clue.text: Hose worn in it?

indicators.note: worn suggests something battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about where you'd put your foot in its stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' scrambles HOSE; the whole clue also describes footwear, which is worn over hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose (stockings) are worn inside footwear, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Journey takes for ever

parts.note: ay (aye) is an old word meaning always or ever

explanation.surface: A trip that seems to last an eternity.
explanation.walkthrough: AY (or aye) as 'ever, always' is a poetic word, as in 'for ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a brief expedition or venture into unfamiliar territory.

clue.text: In 24 hours theologian will be a father

indicators.note: the theologian's letters go in the period of time

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Within a day a religious scholar will become a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: DD (Doctor of Divinity) is the usual crossword theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a familiar, childish word for a dad.

clue.text: Bitterness of ordinary soldier, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is judged by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, not an officer

explanation.surface: A private's resentment reported second-hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent RANKER and RANCOUR sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment, a lasting bitter ill-will.

clue.text: It could stretch into the last ice-age

indicators.note: the answer runs on into the words that follow, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A glacier might reach as far as the most recent glacial period.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic is a material whose main property is that it can be pulled out and spring back.

clue.text: Woman's returned on a ship, that's best

indicators.note: returned means the name with its possessive is read backwards

parts.note: Pru is a woman's name, so 'Woman's' gives PRU'S
SS (steamship) is a standard abbreviation for ship

explanation.surface: A woman comes back aboard a ship and declares it the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns Pru's backwards; 'on' in an across clue means placed after. 'best' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to outdo or exceed them, as a verb.

clue.text: To dish up meal again could be the speciality of the unforthcoming

explanation.surface: Reheating leftovers is apparently the forte of shy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated, it means to serve food a second time; as a noun it is the reticence or restraint shown by quiet people.

clue.text: Drive off holding current toiletry item

indicators.note: the word for chasing away holds the electrical unit inside it

parts.note: shoo is to drive away, as one does a cat
amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A motorist leaves with a bottle of hair wash in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' suggests a car; it means chase away, SHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap product for washing hair.

clue.text: Maybe don't travel enough to suffer

explanation.surface: Staying home too much might be considered a hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as UNDER (insufficiently) + GO (travel); 'Maybe' signals the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words, under-go means go too little; as one word it means endure or experience something unpleasant.

clue.text: Piano is reliable but not grand

explanation.surface: A piano that is dependable but modest in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not grand' tells you which kind of piano: one whose strings run vertically rather than horizontally.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a piano with vertical strings, unlike a grand; an upright person is honest and dependable.

clue.text: Loud crude oath heard

indicators.note: heard signals the word is identified by its spoken sound

parts.note: a raw cuss is a crude swear word

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a vulgar swear word that others can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: RAW (crude) + CUSS (oath) sounds like RAUCOUS in a British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous describes harsh, noisy and disorderly sound.

clue.text: Illiberal support for artist is a comfort

indicators.note: read as 'ill-liberal' this asks for the letter standing for Liberal to be removed

parts.note: an easel supports a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: An intolerant attitude toward funding painters is reassuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illiberal' looks like an adjective; read it as 'without L (Liberal)', taking the L off EASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means relief from pain or worry, a state of comfort.

clue.text: Peer comprehends Arab's blocking

indicators.note: comprehends in its sense of includes, so the looking word holds the abbreviation

parts.note: to pry is to peer nosily
Ar is an abbreviation for Arabic, the Arab's language

explanation.surface: A nobleman understands the Arab's tactic of obstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord but is the verb, PRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A parry is a defensive move in fencing or boxing that wards off a blow, a block.

clue.text: Fellow on American ship causes a to-do

parts.note: USS (United States Ship) prefixes US Navy vessels' names

explanation.surface: A man aboard a US vessel kicks up a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss is a commotion or disturbance, the same as a to-do.

clue.text: Cricketer full of energy is a hit

indicators.note: the cricketer word is filled with the physics letter

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An energetic batsman makes a big shot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'bat' is a batsman, the player who strikes the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat is to strike repeatedly, a synonym of hit.

clue.text: Pack tons into pig

indicators.note: the weight abbreviation goes into the animal word

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
T is the abbreviation for ton or tons

explanation.surface: Load a huge amount of food into a hog.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to put away or load luggage neatly.

clue.text: Concern about five leading division

indicators.note: about here means around, so the worry word goes round the numeral

parts.note: care is concern or worry
V is the Roman numeral for five
up means ahead or leading, as in a score

explanation.surface: Worry about five people at the front of an army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up is a sharing out, typically dishonest, of spoils or territory.

clue.text: Depress poor Ted having to wear robe

indicators.note: the scrambled name is clothed in the garment, which it wears around it

parts.note: a gown is a long robe

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It's sad that unlucky Ted is forced to wear a dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' is the anagram signal for Ted, and 'having to wear' puts that scramble inside the robe, as a person wears clothing around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone down is to make them miserable, i.e. depress them.

clue.text: The point of being in square in rainy Manchester area?

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the weather word

parts.note: wet means rainy
Manchester is in the North West region of England

explanation.surface: What is the purpose of standing in a plaza in drizzly Manchester?
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester, famous for rain, is in England's North West region. 'The point' is a compass point, not purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the sixteen compass bearings, between west and northwest.
